name: Dramatist's Puppet
oracle_text: When this creature enters, for each kind of counter on target permanent, put another counter of that kind on it or remove one from it.
blocked_sentences: When this creature enters, for each kind of counter on target permanent, put another counter of that kind on it or remove one from it.

needs.what: remove_counters accepting counter: {"binding": <kind>} -- remove one counter of the kind a for_each_counter_kind (or choose_counter_kind) bound, so the loop body can be a two-mode choose_mode: add_counters of the bound kind on the target, or remove_counters of the bound kind from it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: for_each_counter_kind plus add_counters with counter: {binding} covers the 'put another' half, but op_remove_counters (without any_kind/all_kinds) reads the kind as str(spec['counter']), so a binding mapping becomes the literal string "{'binding': 'kind'}" and removes nothing; any_kind lets the controller pick any kind on the permanent rather than the iterated kind, and remove_counters_from_among has the same str() read of 'counter'. The loader's bound-kind check does not cover remove_counters either, so the miswrite would load and silently do nothing
